analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md and docs/developer/test.md). Each gets a date bump. prefix-cache.md adds a paragraph at head lines 784-790, and test.md adds a ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests section at head lines 177-211. No executable code, configuration, or mitigation changed, so there is no direct security regression.

The prefix-cache.md paragraph says a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates its destinations already available from host bytes, with no evaluation or fencing. That avoids waiting on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. The import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. The claim concerns T-041 (prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle), TB-007 and A-001. Its security relevance:
- TTFT behavior on cache restore under contention is the basis of the same-account timing channel (SEC-035, accepted risk). Lower restore latency under contention does not change the accepted channel in kind, but it could affect timing observability. A later pass should check this if the corresponding code change is in scope.
- The authentication of the staged file (manifest and whole-file GCM) is stated as unchanged, and the reservation accounting for the host-zero scratch is described as charged. I could not verify this because the implementing source (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift) was not supplied.

The test.md patch excerpt was truncated, but the head hunk range (177-211) is stated as complete. The test uses an env -i sanitized environment, an isolated ephemeral cache and an output report path. It is a test-only, opt-in live benchmark that makes no production change. It reads a user-specified spec path and writes a report atomically. It exposes no secrets and adds no network surface.

The mitigations and assumptions in T-041 (HMAC names, TTL, salt scoping, KEK) are untouched.
